title: Learning to Control Anger When a Colleague Takes Credit
script: Narrator: [tense] During yesterday's meeting, my colleague Bram presented an idea as his own, even though I had explained that exact plan to him privately last week.
Narrator: [frustrated] While he was speaking, I felt my chest tighten, and I had to stop myself from interrupting him in front of our entire department.
Narrator: [honestly] Part of me wanted to correct him immediately, loudly enough that everyone would understand what had actually happened between us.
Narrator: [thoughtful] However, I remembered something my father once told me: reacting in anger rarely fixes the original problem, it usually just creates a second one.
Narrator: [reflective] So instead of speaking up right there, I stayed quiet, took a few slow breaths, and waited until the meeting had ended completely.
Narrator: [determined] Afterward, I asked Bram to speak privately, and even though my hands were still slightly shaking, I kept my voice calm and steady.
Narrator: [calmly] I told him exactly what I had noticed, and I asked him directly why he presented the idea without mentioning where it originally came from.
Narrator: [surprised] To my surprise, he looked genuinely embarrassed and admitted he had been nervous about the presentation and simply forgot to credit me in the moment.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I did not fully believe that explanation, yet I decided that assuming the worst about him would only damage our working relationship further.
Narrator: [reflective] If I had shouted at him during the meeting, he probably would have defended himself instead of actually listening to what I was saying.
Narrator: [honestly] Despite still feeling a little hurt, I accepted his apology, and he promised to mention my contribution clearly in the next department update.
Narrator: [peacefully] Controlling my anger did not erase what happened, but it kept the door open for an honest conversation instead of a lasting conflict between us.
Narrator: [warmly] I am learning that patience under pressure is not weakness; it is choosing a slower, wiser response over a quick, satisfying one.
Narrator: [with a small smile] Bram mentioned my idea properly in this morning's update, and honestly, that felt far better than any argument would have.

quiz.question: What did Bram do during the meeting?
options: He praised the narrator publicly
He presented the narrator's idea as his own
He canceled the meeting
He asked the narrator to present instead
quiz.explanation: Bram presented an idea as his own, even though the narrator had explained that exact plan to him privately the week before.

quiz.question: What did the narrator's father once tell him?
options: Anger always solves problems
Reacting in anger rarely fixes the original problem and usually creates a second one
Never trust colleagues
Silence is always weak
quiz.explanation: He remembered his father's advice that reacting in anger rarely fixes the original problem, it usually creates a second one.

quiz.question: What did the narrator do instead of interrupting during the meeting?
options: He left the room
He stayed quiet, breathed slowly, and waited until the meeting ended
He sent an angry message immediately
He complained to a different colleague
quiz.explanation: He stayed quiet, took slow breaths, and waited until the meeting had ended before addressing it.

quiz.question: How did Bram explain what happened when confronted privately?
options: He denied everything
He said he was nervous and forgot to credit the narrator
He blamed the manager
He refused to talk
quiz.explanation: Bram admitted he had been nervous about the presentation and simply forgot to credit the narrator in the moment.

quiz.question: What does the narrator conclude about patience under pressure?
options: It is a sign of weakness
It is choosing a slower, wiser response over a quick, satisfying one
It means avoiding all conflict permanently
It never actually helps
quiz.explanation: He concludes patience under pressure is not weakness, but choosing a slower, wiser response over a quick one.
